_schema: Ben's review queue. Canonical store; NEEDS_REVIEW.md is the readable mirror. Entry fields: id, title, raised (ISO date), kind, status, source, what, why_it_matters, options (array, only where there is a genuine fork), recommendation, files, resolution (null until Ben answers).
_note: Companion to backlog.json and review.json, NOT a replacement for either.
PURPOSE: things awaiting BEN'S JUDGEMENT. Three kinds live here:
- 'question'        â€” an open call nobody has made yet, usually surfaced by
doing adjacent work. Not blocking, or it would be a
backlog item with blocked_on set.
- 'decision-taken'  â€” a call made ON BEN'S BEHALF so work could continue.
Recorded here so it can be OVERTURNED rather than
quietly becoming precedent. This is the important half:
an unrecorded delegated decision is indistinguishable
from a decision Ben made.
- 'observation'     â€” something noticed in passing that is too small or too
cross-cutting to file, but which a human should see.
- 'novel-work'      â€” raised by a SESSION about its own task (Ben, 2026-08-20):
the work in hand feels NOVEL â€” no owning authority doc, no
saved role or established pattern fits, or it quietly grows
the project's scope. Raise it AT THE MOMENT the feeling
arises, then continue (or pause, if scope growth is large).
Gives Ben a drift detector: novelty should be chosen, not
accreted.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM review.json: review.json is a BLOCKER list â€” items blocked
on a visual artifact only Ben can produce (a mockup, an annotated screenshot).
Work there cannot proceed at all. Entries here are not blocking; they are
questions and reversible calls. If an entry turns out to need a mockup, move it
to review.json and leave a resolution here pointing at it.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM backlog.json: an entry here is not work. If Ben's answer
creates work, file a backlog item and resolve the entry with that item's id.
LIFECYCLE (revised 2026-08-14, Ben's ruling): this file is TRANSIENT â€” a live
queue of open calls, not a permanent audit trail. Append entries as they arise
and set status to 'resolved' with a resolution once answered, exactly as before.
But do NOT let resolved entries accumulate: prune them promptly rather than
holding them for posterity. The reasoning is not lost â€” it lands in code
comments, an authority doc, or a backlog item's design field at the moment the
work happens, and THAT is the durable record. Ben's own framing: 'the docs
should preserve changes made, and the review queue should only be for things
of that level of importance' â€” i.e. open and unresolved, not a history of
everything ever decided. A large housekeeping sweep this date closed 231
entries down to 2 genuinely open ones on this basis.

ARCHIVAL (2026-08-23): 'prune' now means MOVE, not delete. Run node tools/session/archive_reviews.js to move every resolved entry, verbatim, into docs/development/archive/needs-review-<quarter>.json, then re-render the mirror. The hot file holds open entries only.
SEEDED 2026-08-01 at Ben's request, populated from that session.

PURGE 2026-08-23: 240 open entries -> 18. Every entry referring only to backlog ids <= BL-568 (retired by the same-day backlog purge) was retired; 16 more were answered by reading the current docs and tree. All 223 are frozen verbatim in archive/needs-review-purged-2026-08-23.json, each with a resolution saying why. The survivors are asked as a form: tools/session/register/review_queue.js, built by register/build.js, published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/53fb4e56-2eae-439e-bcb7-121fa49bd340 . NR-576 records the calls taken in the sweep.

DRAINED 2026-09-01 on Ben's instruction, from 117 open to 0. The queue had become a shadow backlog: most entries named WORK rather than a judgement, so ten backlog items (BL-713..BL-722) were minted to carry it and every entry was closed with a resolution saying where it went. THE RULE THAT KEEPS IT DRAINED, and it is now in CLAUDE.md Rule 0c: a call only Ben can make belongs here; work belongs in backlog.json; a fact worth remembering belongs in the comment or doc next to the code.

items.title: Two constants taken for the recipe margin anchor - k = 1.0 and typical_workforce = 0.5
items.source: Sprint 31 opening, 2026-09-02: the instrument needed both numbers to run, and neither is in your sentence exactly.
items.what:
1. profit_over_marginal k = 1.0 - your sentence read verbatim: "a greater profit than marginal costs" = margin >= 1.0 x marginal cost, i.e. revenue at least twice marginal cost. The harness prints the roster's count at 0 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 beside it so the bar can move on a measurement (today: ancient 9/2/1/0 of 19, industrial 16/2/2/0 of 25).

2. typical_workforce W = 0.5 for the floor half (M2) - the value corporation_generation.cpp seeds every generated building with (default_workforce_assigned), i.e. the staffing the world opens at. W=1.0 would halve the per-batch share of fixed cost and turn several M2 rows green without any table changing; 0.5 is the honest opening case. Both live in economy.lua's recipe_margin_anchor as data.
items.resolution: RESOLVED. Ben, 2026-09-02: approved as taken - k = 1.0 (profit at least equal to marginal cost) and typical_workforce = 0.5 stand as the authored anchor constants.

items.title: Retune direction for the roster - rates and costs first, or prices?
items.source: recipe_margin first run, 2026-09-02: 41 of 44 priced recipes fail M1, and the failure has a shape - zero or negative value-add before wages, then a 1.50 wage per batch.
items.what:
Three routes to green, not exclusive, and the ORDER is the call:

(a) COSTS AND RATES FIRST (recommended). Processing base_rate 8 batches/tick at W=1 against wage 12 makes wage/batch 1.50 - larger than the entire authored margin of steel (1.0), refined_copper (1.5), silicon (1.0), oil_power (1.58). Raising processing base_rate (or lowering base_wage) shrinks that per-batch term for every recipe at once, and maintenance 10/tick likewise shrinks per batch. Extraction's M2 failure is the same shape: 5 maintenance + 4 wages per tick at W=0.5 against 2.5 x price at the floor. One or two constants move 60+ rows. Risk: throughput changes ripple into the demand/upkeep rates the sweeps just measured.

(b) INPUT QUANTITIES where value-add is zero or negative: steel_from_blooms (22 in, 8 out), consumer_goods (14 in, 12 out), hydroponics_bay (6.25 in, 3 out), food_rations (6 in, 6 out), clean_water (3 in, 3 out), steel_bessemer (8.05 in, 8 out). These are recipe-by-recipe edits and cannot be fixed by (a) alone.

(c) BASE PRICES LAST, up the chain in order, because each tier's price is the next tier's input cost: lifting steel lifts machinery's inputs, and so on to spacecraft_components at 140. The ladder widens, ceil_mult re-derives (haulage_measure), and RESOURCES.md's 56x space premise moves. Doing (c) first is the route that compounds.

Recommendation: (a) then (b), re-run recipe_margin on every edit, (c) only where a row still fails, and re-derive ceil_mult once at the end. Say if you would rather move prices.
items.resolution: RESOLVED. Ben, 2026-09-02: approved the recommended order - rates and costs first, then input quantities where value-add is zero or negative, base prices last with ceil_mult re-derived once at the end. NR-777 records the consequence found on applying it: under k = 1.0 the processing half cannot go green from (a)+(b) alone.

items.title: What is "marginal cost" for a processor - inputs included (A) or conversion only (B)? The reading decides the size of the retune
items.source: Applying NR-776 (approved) to the recipe_margin table, 2026-09-02. With k = 1.0 and inputs inside marginal cost, routes (a)+(b) cannot get a single processing recipe green: profit >= marginal cost means revenue >= 2 x inputs at EVERY stage, so route (c) - prices - is forced on the whole ladder, not the residue.
items.what:
Two readings of Ben's sentence, quantified with the cheapest route setting each good's price, raws pinned at their extraction price, k = 1.0:

A - MARGINAL COST INCLUDES INPUTS (the economics reading, and the one the harness runs today): every processing stage must double the value it takes in. At processing base_rate 16 (wage/batch 0.75): 24 of 50 goods re-priced - steel 8->13.5, machinery 22->55.5, alloys 34->79.5, electronics 29->41.5, spacecraft_components 140->277.5, ordnance 43->110.5, consumer_goods 12->55.5, tools 25.5->88.8 - ladder top 56x -> 111x; 17 alternate routes need their input cost cut to the cheapest route's bar (steel_from_blooms 54.5 -> 6.0, steel_bessemer 13.1 -> 6.0, hydroponics_bay 9.0 -> 0.8, the four construction methods ~25-40%). Every price-dependent tuning moves with it (demand baskets, reservation_mult, procurement lumps, build costs, spawn capital, ceil_mult), the sweeps' baselines go stale, goldens re-bless. In return M2 (fixed cost at the floor) becomes attainable at today's maintenance: steel's value-add 7.5/batch x 8 batches x 0.25 = 15/tick against 16.8 of wages + maintenance - nearly there, and the tiers above clear.

B - MARGINAL COST IS THE CONVERSION COST (wage per batch; inputs pass through at cost): value-add >= 2 x wage. At base_rate 16: 9 goods re-priced by small amounts (food_rations 6->7.5, consumer_goods 12->17, silicon 5->5.5, clean_water 3->4.5), ladder unchanged at 56x, 9 alternates need input cuts (steel_from_blooms 25 -> 6.5, hydroponics_bay 6.3 -> 1.5, charcoal 4.5 -> 2.5; steel's coal route 7.0 -> 6.5 or steel 8 -> 8.5). Cheap - but it leaves gross margins at 10-15% and M2 fails almost everywhere: steel's value-add 2/batch x 8 x 0.25 = 4/tick against 16.8, so the floor half needs maintenance cut ~4x and wages with it - a second, larger retune of the very constant the 2026-09-01 ledger named as 80% of drains.

Either way, processing base_rate 8 -> 16 (wage/batch 1.5 -> 0.75) is route (a) and halves the alternate-route cuts; and EXTRACTION's floor half is independent of the reading: at W = 0.5 a site needs price >= 3.8 to cover 9.5/tick of wages + maintenance at the floor, so raws either rise (iron_ore 2.5 -> ~4, which propagates up under both readings) or extraction's fixed costs fall (maintenance 5 -> ~2, wage 8 -> ~4).

Recommendation: A, with base_rate 16 - it is the sentence as written, it makes profit robust across the whole band rather than only at base, and it is the retune that also clears the floor half without gutting maintenance. It is a sprint, not a pass: one re-priced table, the 17 alternates re-costed, ceil_mult re-derived, sweeps re-baselined. B is the light touch if the 56x ladder must not move.
